fields.title: Model Change as a Product Event
fields.keyTakeaway: A model version is pinned explicitly, a change goes through evals and a traffic split, and the rate of unjustified refusals is a separate criterion that changes between versions.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: The provider released a new version. Should we switch?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: Changing the model changes product behavior imperceptibly: response format, length, tone, behavior in edge cases. Products that switch automatically get regressions that cannot be linked to the cause.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: **[[version-pinning|Version pinning]]** is the first rule of working with providers. Automatic updating means product behavior changes without your involvement and at a moment you didn't choose.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: What changes when changing versions, besides quality:
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: *Format.* The model may start formatting responses differently, breaking parsing. *Length.* A more verbose model breaks UI constraints and increases output cost. *Refusal behavior.* The boundaries of what the model refuses to answer shift between versions. A working feature may start refusing. *Instruction following.* A prompt tuned for one version may work worse on another.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/items/0: Run evals on the new version, compare with current.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/items/1: Check cost and latency on a real profile.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/items/2: Roll out to a traffic fraction, compare product metrics.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/items/3: Switch completely, keeping a rollback option.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: Item 3 is needed because evals measure what we invented, while product metrics measure reality. Covered in `AI2-N4-L2`.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: Separately — **model refusals**. [[refusal|Refusing]] to answer a legitimate request is a product problem, and its frequency varies between versions. It is worth including in evals as a separate criterion: the share of unjustified refusals on normal requests.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: Versions are pinned explicitly. Upgrading is a decision, not an event.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: The first upgrade followed the procedure and revealed two things. Quality per evals grew by 4%. Average response length grew by 40% — the model became more verbose, responses stopped fitting in the card, output cost grew.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: Prompt tweaking with an explicit length constraint restored the format. Without running evals, this would have gone to production.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: Second case: the new version started refusing to answer questions about products with alcohol — previously it answered. The feature for an entire category stopped working. Discovered via evals, added a separate refusal criterion to the suite.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: Fast rollback capability: the version is set in configuration, switching takes a minute. Used once.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Providers drop support for old versions with notice. Pinning delays the decision but does not cancel it — you need a migration plan with a window, as in `IN2-N2-L2`.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: A model version is pinned explicitly, a change goes through evals and a traffic split, and the rate of unjustified refusals is a separate criterion that changes between versions.
